mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a positive supply shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 1% in 1 month, and UNRATE does not rise > 0.5pp
failure_condition: SPX realizes negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the positive supply shock signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, if accompanied by a simultaneous decline in payroll employment, signals a weakening labor market that will drag on consumer spending and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 50k in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances, indicating the labor market deterioration is not immediately impacting equity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, if not already at a restrictive level, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, and starting level < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are positive and significantly higher than baseline returns (t-test p < 0.05) in > 40% of tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating housing market, as measured by rising housing starts, signals increased residential investment that will boost economic growth and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts decline by > 10% within 6 months of the signal, indicating the residential investment impulse was short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the consumer price index, if not accompanied by a rise in industrial production, signals a negative supply shock that will drive inflation higher and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 1% in 1 month, and INDPRO does not rise
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises by > 1% in the following month, but SPX realizes positive 20-day returns, indicating equities are looking through the inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate, if accompanied by rising payroll employment, signals an improving labor market that will boost consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines > 0.2pp and PAYEMS rises > 50k in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 45% of instances where the positive labor market signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate, if already at a low level, signals a preemptive easing of monetary policy that will boost risk appetite and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.5pp in 3 months, and starting level < 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are negative and significantly lower than baseline returns (t-test p < 0.05) in > 40% of easing instances.
